conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion**

Yes, honey can help relieve acute cough symptoms and improve sleep quality in children aged **1 year and older**. 

Systematic reviews demonstrate that honey is more effective at reducing cough frequency and severity than no treatment or diphenhydramine, and performs similarly to common cough suppressants like dextromethorphan. Guidelines from pediatric medical organizations, including the American Academy of Pediatrics, support offering a small dose (2 to 5 mL) of honey as a safe home remedy for coughs from upper respiratory infections in children over 12 months old.

**Critical Safety Warning**

Honey must **never** be given to infants under 12 months of age. Consuming honey before age one carries a high risk of infant botulism, a rare but life-threatening neurological condition caused by bacterial spores.

**Sources**

1. Cochrane Library: https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full
2. PubMed Central: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/
3. HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics): https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/chest-lungs/Pages/Coughs-and-Colds-Medicines-or-Home-Remedies.aspx
4. Cleveland Clinic: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/infant-botulism
